scope: N420 embedded POSIX sign-in terminal preserves UTF8 across read boundaries

baseline.failure: Independent per-read decoding corrupts split valid characters and emits duplicate replacement characters for one truncated sequence.

behavior: One incremental UTF8 decoder per pump; complete text is queued as it becomes available.
EOF and PTY-read OSError both exit the same loop and flush residual bytes exactly once.
Malformed/truncated bytes retain replacement semantics; an incomplete sequence produces one replacement on terminal closure.
ASCII, valid multilingual text, invalid bytes and read-drain idempotence are tested alongside existing cancellation/child/descriptor lifecycle stand-ins.

checks.api_prose: All module/class/function docstrings AST-identical; no new helper, public symbol, signature or API source text
checks.captions: No new user-facing literal; UTF8 codec/error-policy labels are internal protocol strings

limits: POSIX transport correctness and actual local Python stand-ins only; no vendor authentication/browser/account/network operations.
ANSI escape streaming and partial-URL assembly are outside this specific decoding repair.
Windows terminal fallback/native desktop acceptance and whole item420 remain unclaimed.
